mainTopic: How much can witnesses err about the hour? רבא's margins of error for רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, and how הזמה still works within that margin.
overview: The background is a משנה in סנהדרין about two witnesses who disagree on the hour of an event. If one says 'the third hour' and the other says 'the fifth hour,' רבי מאיר invalidates the testimony and רבי יהודה accepts it. The עמוד opens with the end of אביי's explanation: one witness erred by only an hour and a bit. רבא rejects this. The witnesses might have meant times almost three hours apart, and a בית דין may not execute based on a doubt, because the Torah says 'והצילו העדה.' רבא then measures the worst-case gap instead. רבי מאיר allows a mistake of two hours less a bit, and רבי יהודה allows three hours less a bit. The גמרא then brings a משנה and ברייתא: the seven חקירות, including 'which hour,' are essential because testimony that cannot be subject to הזמה is void. This leads to a challenge. If people err by hours, witnesses could always escape הזמה by saying 'we erred.' The answer is that the witnesses get their full margin of error, and הזמה works only if the second witnesses cover that whole window. For רבי מאיר the window runs from hour 1 to the end of hour 5, and for רבי יהודה from hour 1 to the end of hour 6. It does not reach back into the night, because people do not confuse day with night.

steps.title: End of אביי's explanation: one witness erred by an hour and a bit
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes אביי's explanation of רבי יהודה's view. When witnesses say 'third hour' and 'fifth hour,' the event was really in between, and one of them was off by about an hour and a bit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one of them is mistaken by an hour and a little bit.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of אביי's explanation from the previous section. In his view, רבי יהודה accepts testimony of 'third hour' and 'fifth hour' because one witness made a mistake of about an hour and a bit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי pictures the witnesses meaning the end of the third hour and the beginning of the fifth hour. The event really happened at one of those two moments, so one witness was right and the other was off by an hour and a bit. That small mistake is what רבי יהודה is willing to accept.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement. It is the tail end of אביי's explanation that began on the previous amud, and רבא is about to reject it.

phrases.english: and one of them
errs by an hour and a bit.
phrases.notes: The size of the mistake אביי attributes to רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's explanation that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אביי, רבי יהודה accepts testimony where one witness erred by about an hour and a bit.

steps.title: רבא objects: we cannot execute based on a doubtful assumption
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהודה reports אביי's explanation to רבא, and רבא attacks it. If we questioned the witnesses and they meant the beginning of the third hour and the end of the fifth hour, their testimony would contradict and we would not execute. So how can we execute when we simply don't know what they meant?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהודה went and said this teaching before רבא. רבא said: 'Suppose we questioned these witnesses carefully. The one who said three meant the beginning of the third hour, and the one who said five meant the end of the fifth hour. That would be contradicted testimony, and we would not execute. So should we go ahead and execute based on a doubt?!'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי's explanation is brought to רבא, and רבא challenges it. He says אביי's reading depends on guessing that the witnesses meant the times that fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed the witnesses meant end-of-third and start-of-fifth, which is a small gap. But they might have meant start-of-third and end-of-fifth, a gap of almost three hours, which would be עדות מוכחשת. Since we don't know which they meant, accepting the testimony means executing מספק, and רבא says that is unthinkable.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehuda went
phrases.notes: He brings אביי's teaching to רבא.

phrases.english: and said the teaching before Rava.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: וּמָה אִילּוּ דָּיְיקִינַן בְּהָנֵי סָהֲדֵי,
phrases.english: He said: If, were we to examine these witnesses closely,
the one who says three meant the beginning of three,
phrases.notes: The earliest possible meaning of 'third hour.'

phrases.english: and the one who says five meant the end of five,
phrases.notes: The latest possible meaning of 'fifth hour.'

phrases.english: it would be contradicted testimony, and we would not execute,
phrases.notes: The gap would be too large to count as a normal mistake.

phrases.english: so shall we arise and execute based on a doubt?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's explanation completed in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that רבי יהודה only accepts a mistake of an hour and a bit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The witnesses might have meant times nearly three hours apart, which would be contradicted testimony. אביי's reading relies on assuming the favorable case, and a בית דין cannot execute based on that doubt.

steps.title: רבא's verse support: the court must try to save the accused
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports his objection with the פסוק 'ושפטו העדה... והצילו העדה.' The court is commanded to look for ways to save the accused, not to execute based on doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Merciful One said: 'And the congregation shall judge... and the congregation shall save!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his challenge with a פסוק. The Torah tells the judges to try to save the accused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that a בית דין must lean toward saving the accused in capital cases. Executing on the assumption that the witnesses meant the times that fit together is the opposite of what the פסוק demands. This seals the rejection of אביי's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning the Torah / ה׳

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic principle behind much of the leniency in capital cases: a בית דין looks for reasons to acquit, not to convict.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One said:
'And the congregation shall judge' ... 'and the congregation shall save'!
phrases.notes: The court must work to save the accused.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives Torah support to רבא's objection in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a בית דין may not execute based on a doubtful reading of the testimony.

steps.title: רבא's own explanation: how big a mistake each תנא allows
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a new explanation. רבי מאיר holds a person can be off by up to two hours less a bit. רבי יהודה holds a person can be off by up to three hours less a bit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: According to רבי מאיר, a person can be mistaken by two hours less a bit. According to רבי יהודה, a person can be mistaken by three hours less a bit.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected אביי, רבא gives his own rule for how much error each תנא accepts. The next two steps will explain each number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of assuming the smallest possible gap like אביי did, רבא measures the largest possible gap between the witnesses' words. רבי מאיר accepts nearly two hours of error, and רבי יהודה accepts nearly three. Because the worst case is already acceptable, there is no doubt left and the execution is not based on a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (rejects the previous approach and offers a new one)
according to the words / view of

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
According to the words of Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם טוֹעֶה שְׁתֵּי שָׁעוֹת חָסֵר מַשֶּׁהוּ;
phrases.english: a person errs by two hours less a bit;
according to the words of Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם טוֹעֶה שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת חָסֵר מַשֶּׁהוּ.
phrases.english: a person errs by three hours less a bit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected explanation with a new measurement that avoids the problem of ספק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-measuring the allowed error so that the worst case is covered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to אביי, the allowed error was small (a bit, or an hour and a bit), which required assuming the favorable reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר allows two hours less a bit, and רבי יהודה allows three hours less a bit, so even the worst-case reading is acceptable.

steps.title: Explaining רבי מאיר's two hours less a bit
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses say 'second hour' and 'third hour.' The event was either at the beginning of the second hour or at the end of the third hour, so one witness was off by up to two hours less a bit. רבי מאיר accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר, a person errs by two hours less a bit. When the event happened, it was either at the beginning of the second hour or at the end of the third, and one of them erred by two hours less a bit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבא's number fits רבי מאיר's case of 'second hour' and 'third hour.' The farthest apart the witnesses could be is almost two full hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beginning of the second hour to the end of the third hour is nearly two hours. That is the worst case, and רבי מאיר accepts it as a normal human mistake. So he upholds the testimony without relying on any doubt. A gap of 'third' and 'fifth' could be nearly three hours, which is too much for him.

phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם טוֹעֶה שְׁתֵּי שָׁעוֹת חָסֵר מַשֶּׁהוּ,
phrases.english: a person errs by two hours less a bit,
phrases.notes: Restating the rule before explaining it.

phrases.english: when the event happened,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בִּתְחִלַּת שְׁתַּיִם אוֹ בְּסוֹף שָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: it was either at the beginning of two or at the end of three,
and one of them erred
by two hours less a bit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר אָדָם טוֹעֶה שְׁתֵּי שָׁעוֹת חָסֵר מַשֶּׁהוּ מַעֲשֶׂה כִּי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of רבא's rule from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, testimony of 'second' and 'third' hour is valid because the worst-case gap is less than two hours, which is an acceptable mistake.

steps.title: Explaining רבי יהודה's three hours less a bit
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses say 'third hour' and 'fifth hour.' The event was either at the beginning of the third hour or at the end of the fifth hour, so one witness was off by up to three hours less a bit. רבי יהודה accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה, a person errs by three hours less a bit. When the event happened, it was either at the beginning of the third hour or at the end of the fifth, and one of them erred by three hours less a bit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's explanation by applying it to רבי יהודה's case of 'third hour' and 'fifth hour.' The largest possible gap is almost three hours, and רבי יהודה accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers רבא's own objection against אביי. The gap that רבא said would make the testimony contradicted (start of third to end of fifth) is exactly the gap רבי יהודה accepts. Since even the worst case is valid for him, no execution is based on doubt.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the two תנאים disagree about how big a human mistake can be. רבי מאיר allows two hours less a bit, and רבי יהודה allows three hours less a bit. Both are measured by the worst case, so a בית דין never executes based on a guess about what the witnesses meant.

phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם טוֹעֶה שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת חָסֵר מַשֶּׁהוּ,
phrases.english: a person errs by three hours less a bit,
when the event happened

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בִּתְחִלַּת שָׁלֹשׁ אוֹ בְּסוֹף חָמֵשׁ,
phrases.english: it was either at the beginning of three or at the end of five,
phrases.notes: The worst case that רבא raised against אביי.

phrases.english: and one of them erred
by three hours less a bit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָדָם טוֹעֶה שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת חָסֵר מַשֶּׁהוּ מַעֲשֶׂה כִּי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of רבא's rule and closes his explanation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה accepts testimony of 'third' and 'fifth' hour because he allows a mistake of up to three hours less a bit, which covers even the worst-case gap.

steps.title: The seven core questions asked of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: the court questions witnesses with seven חקירות about time and place, including 'which hour.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: they would examine the witness with seven interrogations. In which seven-year cycle? In which year? In which month? On which date of the month? On which day of the week? At which hour? In which place?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a משנה about how judges question witnesses. This sets up the next pieces of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six of the seven questions pin down exactly when the event happened, and the seventh pins down where. 'Which hour' is on the list. That ties this משנה directly to the previous steps about witnesses disagreeing on the hour.

keyTerms.meaning: Core interrogations about the time and place of the event
Here: a seven-year שמיטה cycle, not a week

steps.confusionAlert: Here שָׁבוּעַ does not mean 'week.' It means which seven-year שמיטה cycle within the יובל. The day of the week is asked separately ('בְּאֵיזֶה יוֹם').

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: הָיוּ בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ בְּשֶׁבַע חֲקִירוֹת:
phrases.english: We learned: they would examine him with seven interrogations:
In which seven-year cycle, in which year,
in which month, on which date of the month,
on which day, at which hour,
phrases.notes: 'Which hour' links back to the debate between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about errors in hours.

phrases.english: in which place.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הָיוּ בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ בְּשֶׁבַע חֲקִירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to רבא's large margins of error (steps 4–6). It brings a משנה that makes the hour a required חקירה, and this becomes the basis of the קשיא in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses are questioned on seven points of time and place, including the hour.

steps.title: A ברייתא contrasts core questions with secondary examinations
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one witness saying 'I don't know' to a חקירה voids the testimony. Both witnesses saying 'we don't know' to a בדיקה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: What is the difference between interrogations and examinations? With interrogations, if one of the witnesses says 'I don't know,' their testimony is void. With examinations, even if both say 'we don't know,' their testimony stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets up a contrast between two kinds of questions asked of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חקירות are the seven core time-and-place questions. בדיקות are extra side-detail questions, like the color of clothing. Missing one חקירה, even by just one witness, ruins the testimony. Missing a בדיקה, even by both witnesses, does not.

phrases.english: (And it was taught:) What is the difference between interrogations and examinations?
Interrogations: if one of them said 'I do not know' —
their testimony is void.

phrases.aramaic: בְּדִיקוֹת, אֲפִילּוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם אוֹמְרִים ״אֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִים״ —
phrases.english: Examinations: even if both of them say 'we do not know' —
their testimony stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ruling on what happens when a witness cannot answer the questions listed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not knowing a חקירה voids testimony. Not knowing a בדיקה does not.

steps.title: Why are the two kinds of questions treated differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ברייתא's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: what is different about interrogations, and what is different about examinations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why one 'I don't know' on a חקירה ruins everything, while not knowing a בדיקה does not. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are questions the court asks, and in both cases the witness lacks information. So the sharp difference in outcome needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it / raised a question about it
What is different? Why the distinction?

phrases.english: And we discussed it:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא חֲקִירוֹת וּמַאי שְׁנָא בְּדִיקוֹת?
phrases.english: What is different about interrogations, and what is different about examinations?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוִינַן בַּהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא חֲקִירוֹת וּמַאי שְׁנָא בְּדִיקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason not knowing a חקירה voids testimony while not knowing a בדיקה does not.

steps.title: Missing a core detail makes the testimony impossible to disprove
steps.stepSummary: The answer for חקירות: if a witness doesn't know the time or place, his testimony cannot be subject to הזמה, so it is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said: with interrogations, if one of them says 'I don't know,' their testimony is void, because it becomes testimony that you cannot render זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Without the core time and place, no one can ever prove the witnesses false through הזמה, so the testimony is thrown out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הזמה happens when other witnesses say, 'You were with us somewhere else at that exact time.' That claim only works if the first witnesses committed to a specific time and place. Testimony that can never be exposed this way is not valid testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Proving witnesses false by showing they were elsewhere at the time
Testimony that cannot be subject to הזמה, which is invalid

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the witness seems unreliable. The problem is technical: testimony that can never be exposed through הזמה is disqualified by the תורה.

phrases.english: And we said: interrogations —
if one of them said 'I do not know' —
their testimony is void,
because it becomes testimony
that you cannot render זוממת (prove false through הזמה).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרִינַן: חֲקִירוֹת, אָמַר אֶחָד מֵהֶן אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question for the חקירות side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חקירות are needed for הזמה. Testimony missing them cannot be subject to הזמה and is therefore void.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains why the time of the event, including the hour, is legally essential to testimony. That is the background behind the debate over how far witnesses may err about hours.

steps.title: Missing a side detail still leaves the testimony disprovable
steps.stepSummary: The answer for בדיקות: even without side details, the testimony can still be subject to הזמה, so it remains valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Examinations: it is still testimony that you can render זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. Side details don't matter for הזמה, so not knowing them does not cancel the testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the time and place are fixed, other witnesses can still say 'you were with us elsewhere then.' Details like clothing color play no role in that. So the testimony stays open to הזמה and remains valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony that can be subject to הזמה, and is therefore valid

steps.whatToRemember: The test is הזמה. Details needed to make testimony disprovable (time and place, the חקירות) are essential. Other details (בדיקות) are not essential.

phrases.aramaic: בְּדִיקוֹת, עֵדוּת שֶׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לַהֲזִימָּהּ הִיא.
phrases.english: Examinations: it is testimony that you can render זוממת.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדִיקוֹת, עֵדוּת שֶׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לַהֲזִימָּהּ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by explaining the בדיקות side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בדיקות are not needed for הזמה, so testimony missing them can still be subject to הזמה and stays valid.

steps.title: If people err by hours, no testimony could ever be subject to הזמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if a person can mistake the hour by so much, then the חקירה of 'which hour' becomes testimony that can never be subject to הזמה, because the witnesses will just say 'we erred.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say a person can make such a big mistake, then even the חקירות of 'which hour' would be testimony that you cannot make subject to הזמה, since the witnesses will say: 'We made a mistake!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a strong problem. It uses the rule from steps 10 and 11 together with the idea that people can mistake the hour by several hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said a testimony is void if it cannot be subject to הזמה. Earlier on the דף, we allowed witnesses to be off by a few hours. If so, when a second pair says 'you were with us at that hour,' the first pair can answer 'we got the hour wrong.' That would make every testimony void, which cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: this much, to such an extent
to make it subject to הזמה (prove the witnesses were elsewhere)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the witnesses lie. The problem is that their honest margin of error seems to give them an escape from הזמה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea for the rest of this passage: the margin of error stretches the time period that the second witnesses must cover.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ טָעֵי אִינִישׁ כּוּלֵּי הַאי,
phrases.english: And if you say a person errs that much,
then the interrogations of 'which hour' also

phrases.aramaic: עֵדוּת שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לַהֲזִימָּהּ הִיא,
phrases.english: are testimony that you cannot render subject to הזמה,
since they will say: 'We are mistaken!'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ טָעֵי אִינִישׁ כּוּלֵּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule from step 10 (a testimony that cannot be subject to הזמה is void) to attack the idea that witnesses can err by hours.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim (step 4) that a person can err by two hours less a bit (רבי מאיר) or three hours less a bit (רבי יהודה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a mistake of several hours is allowed, the witnesses can always escape הזמה by claiming an error. Then every testimony is one that cannot be subject to הזמה, and so it would be void.

steps.title: We give the witnesses their whole margin of error
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the witnesses get the full range of their possible error. הזמה works only if the second pair places them elsewhere for that entire range.
steps.simpleTranslation: We give them the entire range of their possible mistakes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem in one short line. The next steps fill in the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Error does not make הזמה impossible. It only widens the time window. If the second witnesses say 'you were with us the whole time, from this hour to that hour,' then the claim 'we erred' no longer helps.

keyTerms.meaning: their mistakes, their margin of error

steps.whatToRemember: Allowing a margin of error does not cancel הזמה. It just means the second witnesses must cover the whole window.

phrases.english: We give them the entire range of their error.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines how הזמה works when there is a margin of error
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since witnesses can always claim an error, הזמה could never work.
steps.terutzMaskana: הזמה works when the second witnesses cover the entire window of possible error.

steps.title: For רבי מאיר, the window is from hour 1 to the end of hour 5
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, witnesses who testified about hour 2 or 3 are given a window from the start of the first hour until the end of the fifth hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר, we give them from the beginning of the first hour until the end of the fifth hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the answer to רבי מאיר's view of how much people err.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is witnesses who said 'hour 2' and 'hour 3.' רבי מאיר allows a mistake of about two hours (step 4), so the window stretches two hours past the third hour, to the end of hour 5. On the early side it stops at the start of hour 1, as the next step explains. To make them subject to הזמה, the second witnesses must say they were with them that whole time.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא who allows a smaller margin of error
the first hour of the day
the end of the fifth hour

phrases.english: According to רבי מאיר:
we give them from the beginning of the first hour
until the end of the fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the step 13 answer according to רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the window for הזמה runs from the start of hour 1 to the end of hour 5.

steps.title: Why the window does not reach back into the night
steps.stepSummary: Logically, the window should start even earlier. But people do not confuse day with night, so it begins at daybreak.
steps.simpleTranslation: By right, we should give them even more time at the beginning. But people do not mistake day for night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question before anyone asks it: why does the window stop at the start of hour 1?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you go back the full margin of error from hour 2, you would land before sunrise. But the witnesses saw the event in daylight, and nobody mixes up day and night. So the window stops at the start of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: by right, logically it should be

steps.confusionAlert: The window is cut short only at the beginning, because of the line between night and day. It is not cut short at the end.

phrases.english: And by right we should give them
more at the beginning,
but between day and night
people do not err.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְדִין הוּא דְּנִיתֵּיב לְהוּ מֵעִיקָּרָא טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the window in step 14 starts at hour 1 and no earlier.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason that limits the window
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The full margin of error should reach back before sunrise.
steps.terutzMaskana: People do not confuse day with night, so the window starts at the beginning of the day.

steps.title: For רבי יהודה, the window is from hour 1 to the end of hour 6
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, who allows a larger margin of error, the window runs from the start of the first hour until the end of the sixth hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יהודה, we give them from the beginning of the first hour until the end of the sixth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now applies the same idea to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that people err by more than רבי מאיר allows. So the window reaches one hour further, to the end of hour 6.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא who allows a larger margin of error
the end of the sixth hour

phrases.english: And according to רבי יהודה:
we give them from the beginning of the first hour
until the end of the sixth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 14, now according to רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the window for הזמה runs from the start of hour 1 to the end of hour 6.

steps.title: For רבי יהודה too, the window should logically start earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that for רבי יהודה, too, the window should by right reach even earlier. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by right we should give them even more time at the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא repeats the same point it made for רבי מאיר, and the explanation comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allows an even bigger margin of error than רבי מאיר. So going back the full margin from the hour they named would reach even further before daybreak. The answer, about day and night, is expected to follow.

phrases.english: And by right we should give them
more at the beginning,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְדִין הוּא דְּנִיתֵּיב לְהוּ מֵעִיקָּרָא טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the step 15 point, now for רבי יהודה. The text physically repeats because it serves a new purpose here.
steps.kashyaTarget: Starting רבי יהודה's window at hour 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His larger margin of error should reach back before the first hour, so why does the window start there?
